speak: October eighteenth, nineteen fifty-eight. Long Island, New York.
sub: October 18, 1958. Long Island, New York.

speak: A physicist who worked on the atomic bomb has a much smaller problem: visitors to his laboratory are getting bored.
sub: A physicist who worked on the atomic bomb has a much smaller problem: visitors to his laboratory are getting bored.

speak: So he connects a computer to a five-inch screen... and draws a ball.
sub: So he connects a computer to a five-inch screen… and draws a ball.

speak: Massive lines begin to form.
sub: Massive lines begin to form.

speak: He never patents it.
sub: He never patents it.

speak: Sixty-eight years later, that dot of light moves more than two hundred billion dollars a year.
sub: Sixty-eight years later, that dot of light moves more than $200 billion a year.

speak: And the entire world is counting down the days for a single game.
sub: And the entire world is counting down the days for a single game.

speak: This is the history of video games.
sub: This is the history of video games.

speak: Chapter one. The game nobody patented.
sub: Chapter 1. The game nobody patented.

speak: It was called Tennis for Two. One line was the court. Another, the net. And a dot of light, the ball.
sub: It was called Tennis for Two. One line was the court. Another, the net. And a dot of light, the ball.

speak: A knob for the angle, a button to hit. Nothing else.
sub: A knob for the angle, a button to hit. Nothing else.

speak: The following year, you could play with the gravity of the Moon... or Jupiter.
sub: The following year, you could play with the gravity of the Moon… or Jupiter.

speak: And afterwards, they dismantled it. The parts went back to the laboratory shelves.
sub: And afterwards, they dismantled it. The parts went back to the laboratory shelves.

speak: But the idea was already out.
sub: But the idea was already out.

speak: In nineteen sixty-two, at M I T, a group of programmers wrote Spacewar: two ships, a star in the middle, torpedoes.
sub: In 1962, at MIT, a group of programmers wrote Spacewar!: two ships, a star in the middle, torpedoes.

speak: It wasn't sold. It was copied. From computer to computer... It was the first game that traveled.
sub: It wasn't sold. It was copied. From computer to computer. It was the first game that traveled.

speak: Chapter two. The coin box.
sub: Chapter 2. The coin box.

speak: Ralph Baer was an engineer with a question: if almost every home had a television... why was it only used for watching?
sub: Ralph Baer was an engineer with a question: if almost every home had a television… why was it only used for watching?

speak: By nineteen sixty-eight he had a prototype. In nineteen seventy-two it went on sale as the Magnavox Odyssey: the first home console.
sub: By 1968 he had a prototype. In 1972 it went on sale as the Magnavox Odyssey: the first home console.

speak: One of its games was ping-pong. A young man named Nolan Bushnell tried it at a demonstration. Weeks later, he founded Atari.
sub: One of its games was ping-pong. A young man named Nolan Bushnell tried it at a demonstration. Weeks later, he founded Atari.

speak: His engineer, Al Alcorn, built his own version inside a wooden cabinet. They left it in a California bar, just to see what would happen.
sub: His engineer, Al Alcorn, built his own version inside a wooden cabinet. They left it in a California bar, just to see what would happen.

speak: A few days later they got a call: the machine wasn't working.
sub: A few days later they got a call: the machine wasn't working.

speak: Alcorn opened it up. It wasn't broken... It was overflowing with coins.
sub: Alcorn opened it up. It wasn't broken. It was overflowing with coins.

speak: It was called Pong.
sub: It was called Pong.

speak: Chapter three. The fever and the burial.
sub: Chapter 3. The fever and the burial.

speak: In nineteen seventy-seven, Atari launched a cartridge console: one machine, all the games you could want.
sub: In 1977, Atari launched a cartridge console: one machine, all the games you could want.

speak: Arcades filled with lights and noise. By nineteen eighty-three, home video games were generating three point two billion dollars in the United States.
sub: Arcades filled with lights and noise. By 1983, home video games were generating $3.2 billion in the United States.

speak: And then, everything came crashing down.
sub: And then, everything came crashing down.

speak: Too many consoles. Too many rushed games. People lost trust... and stopped buying.
sub: Too many consoles. Too many rushed games. People lost trust… and stopped buying.

speak: In September nineteen eighty-three, Atari trucks dumped unsold cartridges of E. T. and other games into a landfill in the New Mexico desert.
sub: In September 1983, Atari trucks dumped unsold cartridges of E.T. and other games into a landfill in the New Mexico desert.

speak: By nineteen eighty-five, the market had plunged nearly ninety-seven percent.
sub: By 1985, the market had plunged nearly 97%.

speak: Analysts said it was just a fad... And that it was over.
sub: Analysts said it was just a fad. And that it was over.

speak: Chapter four. The Trojan horse.
sub: Chapter 4. The Trojan horse.

speak: On the other side of the world, Nintendo had been selling a family console since nineteen eighty-three: the Famicom.
sub: On the other side of the world, Nintendo had been selling a family console since 1983: the Famicom.

speak: It wanted to reach the United States. But there, after the crash, stores didn't even want to hear the words video game.
sub: It wanted to reach the United States. But there, after the crash, stores didn't even want to hear the words video game.

speak: So Nintendo didn't sell a video game... It sold a toy.
sub: So Nintendo didn't sell a video game. It sold a toy.

speak: They changed its shape, changed its name, and packed a robot next to it. On October eighteenth, nineteen eighty-five, they tested it in New York.
sub: They changed its shape, changed its name, and packed a robot next to it. On October 18, 1985, they tested it in New York.

speak: Exactly twenty-seven years after Tennis for Two.
sub: Exactly twenty-seven years after Tennis for Two.

speak: Among its games was one starring a plumber. Super Mario Bros sold over forty million copies.
sub: Among its games was one starring a plumber. Super Mario Bros. sold over 40 million copies.

speak: And in nineteen eighty-nine, Nintendo put video games in your pocket: the Game Boy. With Tetris in the box.
sub: And in 1989, Nintendo put video games in your pocket: the Game Boy. With Tetris in the box.

speak: Chapter five. The betrayal.
sub: Chapter 5. The betrayal.

speak: In the early nineties, Sony and Nintendo were working together on a C D drive for the Super Nintendo.
sub: In the early nineties, Sony and Nintendo were working together on a CD drive for the Super Nintendo.

speak: In nineteen ninety-one, Nintendo announced it would build it... with Philips.
sub: In 1991, Nintendo announced it would build it… with Philips.

speak: At Sony, many wanted to move on. One engineer, Ken Kutaragi, did not.
sub: At Sony, many wanted to move on. One engineer, Ken Kutaragi, did not.

speak: On December third, nineteen ninety-four, Sony launched its own console in Japan. It used C Ds. It bet everything on three D.
sub: On December 3, 1994, Sony launched its own console in Japan. It used CDs. It bet everything on 3D.

speak: It was called PlayStation. It sold over one hundred and two million units.
sub: It was called PlayStation. It sold over 102 million units.

speak: Nintendo had lost a partner... And gained a rival.
sub: Nintendo had lost a partner. And gained a rival.

speak: Chapter six. The open city.
sub: Chapter 6. The open city.

speak: In the year two thousand came the PlayStation two. Beyond games, it played D V Ds, right as D V D became the standard for movies.
sub: In the year 2000 came the PlayStation 2. Beyond games, it played DVDs, right as DVD became the standard for movies.

speak: It sold over one hundred and sixty million units: even today, it remains the best-selling console in history.
sub: It sold over 160 million units: even today, it remains the best-selling console in history.

speak: And in October two thousand and one, an Edinburgh studio released a game that changed the rules: Grand Theft Auto three.
sub: And in October 2001, an Edinburgh studio released a game that changed the rules: Grand Theft Auto III.

speak: An entire city, in three D, where you could go anywhere you wanted. It was no longer a level. It was a world.
sub: An entire city, in 3D, where you could go anywhere you wanted. It was no longer a level. It was a world.

speak: Remember that name. It will return.
sub: Remember that name. It will return.

speak: Chapter seven. Everyone plays.
sub: Chapter 7. Everyone plays.

speak: In two thousand and six, the Wii did the unthinkable: it got people playing who had never touched a controller. Grandparents. Parents. Kids. Everyone swinging their arm in front of the T V.
sub: In 2006, the Wii did the unthinkable: it got people playing who had never touched a controller. Grandparents. Parents. Kids. Everyone swinging their arm in front of the TV.

speak: Over one hundred and one million consoles.
sub: Over 101 million consoles.

speak: Then came smartphones. Today, more than half of the industry's revenue comes from a screen we carry in our pocket.
sub: Then came smartphones. Today, more than half of the industry's revenue comes from a screen we carry in our pocket.

speak: In two thousand and eleven, a game made of blocks left beta behind. Minecraft. Over three hundred and fifty million copies: the best-selling game in history.
sub: In 2011, a game made of blocks left beta behind. Minecraft. Over 350 million copies: the best-selling game in history.

speak: And on September seventeenth, two thousand and thirteen, that name returned. G T A five.
sub: And on September 17, 2013, that name returned. GTA V.

speak: In three days it grossed one billion dollars... No movie, no album, no entertainment product had ever done it that fast.
sub: In three days it grossed $1 billion. No movie, no album, no entertainment product had ever done it that fast.

speak: Chapter eight. Thirteen years.
sub: Chapter 8. Thirteen years.

speak: In two thousand and seventeen, the Nintendo Switch erased the line between home console and handheld.
sub: In 2017, the Nintendo Switch erased the line between home console and handheld.

speak: It has sold over one hundred and fifty-seven million units: less than three million away from catching the PlayStation two.
sub: It has sold over 157 million units: less than three million away from catching the PlayStation 2.

speak: Its successor, the Switch two, sold three and a half million in its first four days. No Nintendo console had ever launched that fast.
sub: Its successor, the Switch 2, sold 3.5 million in its first four days. No Nintendo console had ever launched that fast.

speak: In two thousand and twenty-five, the industry surpassed two hundred billion dollars for the first time.
sub: In 2025, the industry surpassed $200 billion for the first time.

speak: And meanwhile, G T A five never stopped selling: over two hundred and thirty million copies.
sub: And meanwhile, GTA V never stopped selling: over 230 million copies.

speak: Its successor was announced. Delayed once. And again.
sub: Its successor was announced. Delayed once. And again.

speak: Now it has a date: November nineteenth, two thousand and twenty-six. Thirteen years later.
sub: Now it has a date: November 19, 2026. Thirteen years later.

speak: It all started with a dot of light on a five-inch screen, so lab visitors don't get bored. Today, it is an entire city.
sub: It all started with a dot of light on a five-inch screen, so lab visitors don't get bored. Today, it is an entire city.

speak: And the next chapter of this story... is about to begin.
sub: And the next chapter of this story… is about to begin.
